title: Microsoft Purview DLP: restrict access to Fabric semantic models and lakehouses
summary: Hold: both portal paths omit intermediate wizard pages named in Microsoft's configuration instructions. The roadmap dates, opt-in default, licensing, billing explanation and documented limitations are supported; the differing preview and general availability statements are reported rather than silently reconciled.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a DLP restrict access action for Fabric semantic models and lakehouses.
claims.quote: DLP restrict access action allows you to block access to guest users or all users depending on what labels or sensitive information types matches your semantic models or lakehouses.

claims.claim: The action can block guests or all users based on matching sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: Semantic-model DLP evaluation is skipped for publish, republish or refresh initiated using service principal authentication.
claims.quote: DLP evaluation of the semantic model doesn't occur if either of the following is true: An account using service principal authentication initiates the event (publish, republish, on-demand refresh, scheduled refresh).

claims.claim: Semantic-model DLP evaluation is skipped when the owner is a service principal.
claims.quote: DLP evaluation of the semantic model doesn't occur if either of the following is true: ... The semantic model owner is a service principal.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Configured actions run automatically on a policy match, so an ordinary refresh can cause access restrictions without a new approval.

claims.quote: Data Loss Prevention policy: A tenant has 10 Fabric workspaces, each with 50 assets. The policy only applies to five of these Fabric workspaces. The asset count for this policy is 250.

claims.claim: The printed creation path gives the intervening pages and sections needed to reach the restrict access action.
claims.quote: The Define policy settings page appears. Choose Create or customize advanced DLP rules ... On the Customize advanced DLP rules page ... Select Create rule.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Assign admin units > Fabric and Power BI workspaces > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Actions > Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations'. State in the row note: 'Name and describe the policy after choosing Custom policy, then select Next; on Assign admin units, select Next without assigning units.' These intermediate pages are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/governance/data-loss-prevention-configure.

claims.claim: The printed New-DlpComplianceRule call is a documented general DLP rule creation call with a sensitive-information condition and BlockAccess action, not a confirmed Fabric-specific example.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name "SocialSecurityRule" -Policy "USFinancialChecks" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name="U.S. Social Security Number (SSN)"} -BlockAccess $True

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule belongs to Security & Compliance PowerShell and its cited blocking example is generic rather than Fabric-specific.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... The rule checks for social security numbers and blocks access if it finds them.

claims.claim: The printed workspace-scoping creation path proceeds directly from Custom policy to Fabric and Power BI workspaces and Edit.
claims.quote: Name the policy and provide a meaningful description. When done, select Next. ... Select Next when you get to the Assign admin units page. ... Select Fabric and Power BI workspaces as the location
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Assign admin units > Fabric and Power BI workspaces > Edit'. State in the row note: 'Name and describe the policy after choosing Custom policy, then select Next; on Assign admin units, select Next without assigning units.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/governance/data-loss-prevention-configure.

claims.claim: The New-DlpCompliancePolicy call enables a policy for all qualifying Power BI workspaces with a workspace-ID exception, subject to the row's documented Premium Gen2 qualification.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "PowerBIPolicy" -Comment "Primary policy" -PowerBIDlpLocation "All" -PowerBIDlpLocationException "workspaceID1","workspaceID2","workspaceID3" -Mode Enable

claims.claim: The policy cmdlet reference describes Premium Gen2 Power BI workspaces, while neither cited cmdlet reference names Fabric lakehouses or semantic models.
claims.quote: The PowerBIDlpLocation parameter specifies the Power BI workspace IDs to include in the DLP policy. Only workspaces hosted in Premium Gen2 capacities are permitted. You can use the value All to include all supported workspaces.

claims.claim: Administrators can monitor Fabric DLP policy-match alerts on the Alerts page in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: If you enable alerts in the policy, an alert records on the data loss prevention Alerts page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Activity explorer can display Fabric and Power BI DLP data.
claims.quote: You can view data from DLP for Fabric and Power BI in Activity explorer.

claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly settle whether service-principal changes to lakehouses receive restrict access evaluation.
claims.quote: Searched: Fabric lakehouse DLP service principal evaluation restrict access; "Fabric" "DLP" "lakehouse" "service principal" evaluation. Read overview and troubleshooting: semantic-model exceptions and a mirrored-database SPN case, but no lakehouse-specific SPN rule.
